items.summary: GPU tile_fft for non-power-of-two sizes on HIP: without libmathdx the GPU path supports only power-of-two sizes divisible by block_dim and raises ValueError otherwise (builtins.py:13435-13448); ROCm has no device-callable FFT, so closing the gap means an in-tree Bluestein or direct-DFT path upstream does not have

decided.note: 2026-11-18: defer, ship upstream's no-libmathdx behaviour in 1.14.0+rocm.0 and name the gap in the release notes

items.summary: Conditional graph nodes on HIP: capture_if/capture_while inside a graph capture need cudaGraphAddNode conditional nodes (CUDA 12.4+), which HIP 7.14 does not have; the port reports them unsupported as upstream does for older CUDA. Adopt native HIP conditional nodes if ROCm ever ships them

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report unsupported on HIP exactly as upstream does for old CUDA; HIP's plans are unknown and it may be a hardware limitation, so not expected soon

items.summary: Clang/LLVM GPU compiler options on HIP: wp.config.llvm_cuda (kernels JIT-compiled by the bundled Clang/LLVM instead of the vendor runtime compiler) and the --clang-build-toolchain build option are NVPTX-only; the bundled LLVM has no AMDGPU target. The port makes both fail with a clear error on HIP. Supporting them would mean building and shipping LLVM with the AMDGPU backend and ROCm device libraries; hipRTC is already Clang-based, so there is no known AMD use case

decided.note: 2026-11-18: do not port it in this line, and make both switches fail clearly instead of misbehaving

items.summary: rocPRIM 4.8 (ROCm 10.2 rocm-sdk wheels), gfx950: hipcub::DeviceRadixSort::SortKeys on uint64_t keys returns output that is not sorted by the selected bits when end_bit == 64 and begin_bit > 0 (tested 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 31, 32, 33, 40) for more than 1024 keys; [0,64), [0,63), [1,63), [16,48), [32,56), [32,63) are correct. cuBQL's GPU builders sort {primID,nodeID} with bits [32,64), so leaves with several primitives were built wrong (Warp test_mesh_query_ray_count_intersections, cubql leaf size 4, 1337/5000 rays). Port works around it by sorting [0,64) under __HIPCC__ in the vendored sah_builder.h; sm_builder.h, elh_builder.h and rebinMortonBuilder.h (not used by Warp) have the same [32,64) sort, and upstream cuBQL's HIP path is affected too

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; standalone reproducer and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx950: hipMallocAsync on the null stream (0) while another stream of the device is being captured in global mode segfaults inside libamdhip64 instead of returning an error (CUDA returns cudaErrorStreamCaptureImplicit). Seen through cuBQL's refit, which ran on stream 0 during a Warp graph capture (mesh with bvh_constructor=cubql, refit inside wp.ScopedCapture). The port now passes Warp's current stream to cuBQL's refit, which avoids the null stream; the HIP crash itself is unfixed

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; standalone reproducer and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx950: hipModuleOccupancyMaxPotentialBlockSize suggests 1024 threads for a hipRTC-compiled kernel declared __launch_bounds__(128), whose hipFuncGetAttribute(HIP_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK) is 128; a launch with the suggested size would fail. Passing the attribute as blockSizeLimit gives 128 (grid 4096). The port clamps the limit in its occupancy wrapper (cuda_util.cpp)

decided.note: 2026-11-18: report it; standalone reproducer and draft first, Jeff files

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), 2x gfx942: a captured hipMemcpyAsync between pinned host memory and memory allocated in the same capture (hipMallocAsync) makes hipGraphInstantiateWithFlags return hipErrorNotSupported (801) unless the capture device is 0 and the pinned buffer was allocated with device 0 current (D2H also works when both are device 1); on capture device 0 with the pinned buffer allocated on device 1, H2D segfaults the process. Copies to plain hipMalloc memory are unaffected. Warp's in-capture tests on a non-primary ordinal (test_sparse and test_fem_integrate test_capturability_cuda_1, test_graph test_cuda_graph_alloc_transient_stream_cuda_1) fail with error 801 in wp_cuda_graph_create_exec; the earlier AMD port hid this by limiting those tests to ordinal 0. Standalone reproducer h2d2.hip and the full matrix in the notes

HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), 2x gfx942: hipMemPoolSetAccess on device 0's default pool grants peer access to device 1 (hipMemAccessFlagsProtReadWrite, hipMemPoolGetAccess then reports 3) but revoking it with hipMemAccessFlagsProtNone returns hipErrorInvalidDevice (101), with or without outstanding allocations, and access stays granted. CUDA documents ProtNone as revoking access. Warp's wp_cuda_set_mempool_access_enabled is correct; test_mempool_access and test_unified_memory's mempool-state peer test fail on it (error 101, Failed to disable memory pool access). Standalone reproducer poolacc.hip in the notes

HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), 2x gfx942: a stream capture that forks from a device-0 stream to a device-1 stream and launches a kernel on each device makes hipGraphInstantiate return hipErrorNotSupported (801); the same capture with kernels on device 0 only (with or without a peer copy from device 1) instantiates. CUDA supports kernel nodes for several devices in one graph. Warp's test_streams test_stream_arg_graph_mgpu and test_stream_scope_graph_mgpu fail on it once peer access is detected (they skip on hosts where Warp's IOMMU heuristic reports no peer-to-peer). Report as a defect, or record as a documented limitation if HIP declares it one. Standalone reproducer mdev.hip described in the notes

AMD clang 24 (ROCm 10.2 wheels, hipRTC and offline -O3), gfx950: when one function computes __fsqrt_rn(x) (llvm.sqrt.f32 with !fpmath 3.0, the approximate native sqrt) and sqrtf(x) (llvm.sqrt.f32 without !fpmath, correctly rounded) of the same value, EarlyCSE merges the two calls and keeps the !fpmath tag, so sqrtf becomes the approximation: 2535452 of the 16777216 floats in [1,4) off by 1 ulp, against 0 when sqrtf is alone or at -O0. The merged call should drop !fpmath (the most generic of the two). Seen through a Warp user snippet that used both; Warp's own wp.sqrt is unaffected unless a snippet in the same function uses __fsqrt_rn. Standalone reproducer sq3.hip in the notes; not checked against upstream LLVM main

HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx1100 (W7800): hipDrvMemcpy3DAsync and the runtime hipMemcpy3DAsync from pageable (malloc) host memory into a hipArray still read the host buffer after the call returns: overwriting the buffer right after the call and then synchronizing leaves every element of the array with the overwritten value (1D w=32/256/4096, 2D 2x2/64x64/1024x1024; runtime API 2048 of 2048 wrong). Linear hipMemcpyAsync H2D stages pageable memory correctly (0 bad). CUDA stages pageable memory before an async copy returns, and Warp relies on that: textures built from NumPy data had their first 16 bytes replaced by glibc free-list pointers once the temporary host copy was freed. Warp now synchronizes the stream after a host-side 3D copy outside a capture. Reproducer m3d_pageable.cpp in the notes

items.summary: HIP 7.17 (ROCm 10.2 wheels), gfx1100 (W7800): hipDrvMemcpy3DAsync on a stream capturing in global mode returns success but copies immediately and adds no node to the graph (device->array->device: graph has 0 nodes, the copy has happened before instantiation, a replay after changing the source copies nothing, 2048 of 2048 wrong). The runtime hipMemcpy3DAsync captures correctly (2 memcpy nodes, replays right, all three capture modes, 1 and 4 channels). Related: hipArray3DGetDescriptor returns hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported during a global capture and invalidates it. Warp now routes its 3D texture copies through hipMemcpy3DAsync with element sizes recorded at array creation. Reproducer m3d_capture.cpp in the notes
